## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dutiyapīṭhavimānavatthu* ("Second Throne Mansion", Vv 2) is a short canonical poem preserved in the *Vimānavatthu* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. Reflecting the standard thematic core of the collection, the narrative centers on the principle that acts of giving invariably yield fruitful karmic results in heavenly rebirths.

 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates significant Pali-internal formulaic reuse across 26 texts, consisting of 160 matching segments [DharmaNexus]. It shares nearly identical structural framing and verses with its neighboring texts, particularly the *Paṭhamapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 1), *Tatiyapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 3), and *Catutthapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 4), as well as other mansion accounts including the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Dīpavimānavatthu* (Vv 9), and *Uttarāvimānavatthu* (Vv 15) [DharmaNexus]. Its verses are commented upon in detail throughout the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* and share formulaic lines with the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus additionally records weak, non-curated alignments with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and the Tibetan *Lalitavistara* (D 95), reflecting incidental formulaic similarities rather than direct historical parallels [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
